histo1.text: This section is taken from which structure?
histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Sagittal section of the lip showing 3 distinct zones: the outer thin skin surface with hair follicles and sebaceous glands, the central core of skeletal muscle (orbicularis oris), and the inner mucosal surface lined by stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium with submucosal labial glands.
histo1.keyConcept: Lip histology: Thin skin, orbicularis oris muscle core, and oral mucosa.

histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Structure 1 represents the external cutaneous (skin) surface, covered by keratinized stratified squamous epithelium with hair follicles, sebaceous glands, and sweat glands.
Criteria of Identification: Structure 2 shows hair follicles embedded in the dermis with associated sebaceous glands on the cutaneous surface.
Criteria of Identification: Structure 3 is the central muscle core formed by striated skeletal muscle fibers of the orbicularis oris muscle cut in cross and longitudinal sections.

Criteria of Identification: Structure 4 is the vermilion zone (red margin of the lip), the transition zone covered by modified translucent stratified squamous epithelium with tall, highly vascular dermal papillae close to the surface.
histo1.keyConcept: Vermilion border (red margin): Translucent epithelium with rich capillary loops.

histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Submucosal mixed/mucous labial salivary glands embedded in connective tissue.
Criteria of Identification: The inner oral aspect is lined by moist, thick, non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium.
Criteria of Identification: Group of mixed, predominantly mucous tubuloacinar labial glands situated in the submucosa.
Criteria of Identification: Striated skeletal muscle bundles of the orbicularis oris constituting the muscular framework of the lip.
Criteria of Identification: Submucosal labial salivary glands.
Criteria of Identification: Internal oral mucosa lined by stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium.
Criteria of Identification: Vermilion border displaying high dermal vascular papillae.

histo1.text: This section is taken from which structure?
histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Mass of interlacing skeletal muscle bundles covered by mucous membrane exhibiting characteristic dorsal lingual papillae.
histo1.keyConcept: Tongue histology: Interlacing skeletal muscle with specialized dorsal papillae.

histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Numerous conical, pointed papillae covered by keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, lacking taste buds.
histo1.keyConcept: Filiform papillae: Most numerous, conical, keratinized, purely mechanical (no taste buds).

histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Bundles of skeletal muscle fibers arranged in three planes (longitudinal, transverse, and vertical).
Criteria of Identification: Dense irregular collagenous connective tissue supporting the lingual epithelium.
Criteria of Identification: Serous and mucous lingual salivary glands embedded among the muscle bundles.

histo1.text: Which type of lingual papilla is shown?
histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large, dome-shaped papilla surrounded by a deep circular furrow (moat) containing numerous lateral taste buds and receiving ducts of von Ebner serous glands.
histo1.keyConcept: Circumvallate papilla: Large, sunken in moat, lateral taste buds, von Ebner serous glands at base.

histo1.text: What do the arrows at the bottom point to?
histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Purely serous von Ebner glands located in the lamina propria whose watery secretion washes the circular moat around circumvallate papillae.
histo1.keyConcept: Von Ebner glands: Purely serous glands flushing circumvallate grooves.

histo1.text: Which type of lingual papilla is shown?
histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Slender, conical, keratinized spires.

histo1.text: Which type of lingual papilla is shown?
histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Mushroom-shaped papilla with a narrow neck and expanded dome-shaped head covered by non-keratinized epithelium with taste buds on its dorsal surface.
histo1.keyConcept: Fungiform papillae: Mushroom-shaped with apical taste buds.

histo1.text: Which type of lingual papilla is shown?
histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Broad papilla surrounded by deep trench lined by taste buds.

histo1.text: What is the structure outlined by the dashed line?
histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Pale-staining, barrel-shaped intraepithelial sensory organ opening via an apical taste pore.
histo1.keyConcept: Taste bud: Barrel-shaped sensory organ containing gustatory, supporting, and basal cells.

histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Small apical opening through which sensory microvilli contact dissolved tastants.

histo1.text: What do the arrows labeled 2 point to?
histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Small rounded regenerative stem cells located at the base of the taste bud.
histo1.keyConcept: Basal cells: Regenerative stem cell population of taste bud.

histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Underlying connective tissue stroma.

histo1.text: What is shown in this image?
histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Rounded acini with narrow lumina, basophilic basal cytoplasm (rich in RER), spherical basal nuclei, and apical eosinophilic zymogen granules.
histo1.keyConcept: Serous acini: Spherical, basophilic base, round central/basal nucleus, narrow lumen.

histo1.text: What is shown in this image?
histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Tubular/rounded acini with wide lumina, pale foamy cytoplasm filled with mucigen droplets, and flattened nuclei compressed against the basement membrane.
histo1.keyConcept: Mucous acini: Wide lumen, pale vacuolated cytoplasm, flattened peripheral basal nuclei.

histo1.text: What is the structure enclosed by the circle?
histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Mucous acinus capped by a crescent-shaped hood of serous cells (serous demilune of Giannuzzi).
Criteria of Identification: Crescentic cap of serous cells surmounting a mucous tubule.

histo1.text: What do the lines at the center of the circle point to?
histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Central secretory lumen of the acinus.

histo1.text: What type of acini is shown?
histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Conspicuous mixed acinar architecture with serous crescents.
Criteria of Identification: Crescent of Giannuzzi.

histo1.text: What do the lines at the bottom point to?
histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Pale pyramidal cells with flattened basal nuclei.

histo1.text: Which structure is shown in this SEM photomicrograph?
histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) showing characteristic curved horn-like, keratinized filiform papillae.

histo1.text: What is the structure outlined in yellow?
histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Taste bud outlined in yellow on the lateral wall of vallate papilla.
histo1.keyConcept: Taste bud: Barrel-shaped sensory organ containing gustatory and supporting cells.

histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Apical taste pore opening onto the epithelial surface.
histo1.keyConcept: Taste pore: Apical orifice admitting chemical tastants to receptor microvilli.

histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Sustentacular supporting cells.

histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Short pyramidal stem cells at the base.
histo1.keyConcept: Basal stem cells giving rise to taste bud cell turnover.

histo1.text: The cell outlined in yellow belongs to which structure?
histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: TEM of serous acinar cell showing extensive parallel stacks of rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) in the basal region and dense apical zymogen granules.
histo1.keyConcept: Ultrastructure of serous cell: Basal RER + apical electron-dense zymogen granules.

histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Transmission electron micrograph of a mucous acinar cell. Structure 1 points to the apical cytoplasm filled with numerous large, pale, electron-lucent membrane-bound mucin droplets that push the nucleus against the basal plasma membrane.
histo1.keyConcept: Mucous cell TEM: Apical cytoplasm packed with pale, electron-lucent mucin granules.

histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Rounded euchromatic nucleus located basally.
histo1.keyConcept: Serous cell nucleus: Spherical euchromatic basal nucleus.

histo1.text: The cell outlined in yellow belongs to which structure?

histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Light, electron-lucent membrane-bound mucin droplets.

histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Flattened nucleus compressed against the basal plasma membrane.

histo1.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Apical acinar lumen where secretory products are discharged.

histo2.text: Identify the cell shown in this TEM photo.
histo2.explanation: Criteria of Identification: TEM of parietal (oxyntic) cell showing prominent intracellular secretory canaliculi lined by microvilli, extensive tubulovesicular system, and innumerable large mitochondria (supplying ATP for H+/K+ ATPase acid pump).

histo2.text: Identify the cell shown in this TEM photo.
histo2.explanation: Criteria of Identification: TEM of peptic (chief) cell demonstrating abundant parallel arrays of rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) in the basal cytoplasm and apical electron-dense zymogen granules containing pepsinogen.
histo2.keyConcept: Chief cell ultrastructure: Extensive basal RER, supranuclear Golgi, apical zymogen granules.

histo2.text: Identify the cell shown in this TEM photo.
histo2.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Closed enteroendocrine cell: rests on the basement membrane but does NOT reach the luminal surface; contains membrane-bound neurosecretory granules concentrated in the basal cytoplasm near capillary fenestrae.
histo2.keyConcept: Closed enteroendocrine cell: Does not contact lumen; basal endocrine granules.

histo2.text: Identify the cell shown in this TEM photo.
histo2.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Open enteroendocrine cell: has a narrow apical cytoplasmic process equipped with microvilli reaching the intestinal lumen to sample luminal chemical contents (chemoreceptor).
histo2.keyConcept: Open enteroendocrine cell: Apical process contacts lumen (luminal chemosensor).

histo2.text: Identify the cell shown in this TEM photo.
histo2.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Pyramidal cell situated at the base of intestinal crypts containing large, brightly refractile apical secretory granules rich in lysozyme, defensins, and zinc.
